question: Should OpenClaw add native child-session context-pressure notification/recovery, and what threshold, notification target, and recovery action semantics should it use?
rationale: Current source exposes the necessary pressure and lineage facts, but the issue requests new policy for thresholds, parent/operator signaling, and recovery actions that is not defined by existing docs or tests.

options.title: Add alert-only session pressure diagnostics
options.body: Use existing contextBudgetStatus and parentSessionKey/spawnedBy lineage to surface parent/operator alerts first, leaving recovery as an explicit later decision.

options.title: Add alert plus controlled recovery
options.body: Define an opt-in recovery contract that can compact, rotate, or reroute a saturated child session after notifying the parent/operator.

options.title: Keep reporting-only behavior
options.body: Decline native orchestration policy for now and document that fleets should monitor context pressure externally using gateway/session status data.

recommendation.title: Add alert-only session pressure diagnostics
recommendation.body: Use existing contextBudgetStatus and parentSessionKey/spawnedBy lineage to surface parent/operator alerts first, leaving recovery as an explicit later decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses session health, subagent architecture, and gateway-facing behavior, and current local history points to Peter Steinberger as the broad recent owner of those surfaces.
